examples.en: The taekwondo athlete smashed bricks with his hand.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 결승에서 강한 상대를 격파했어요.
examples.en: Our team crushed a strong opponent in the final.

examples.ko: 그는 송판 세 장을 한 번에 격파해요.
examples.en: He breaks three boards at once.
I finally defeated the last boss in the game.

examples.ko: 시범에서 발차기로 나무판을 격파하는 모습이 멋있었어요.
examples.en: It looked cool when he broke the wooden board with a kick in the demonstration.

examples.ko: 군대가 적의 방어선을 격파했다는 기록이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a record that the army broke through the enemy's defense line.

explain: '부수다'와 달리 태권도 시범에서 송판이나 벽돌을 깰 때, 또는 경기나 게임에서 강한 상대를 눌러 이길 때 써요. 일상에서 물건을 부술 때는 '부수다', '깨다'를 써요.
explain_en: Unlike '부수다', it is used for breaking boards or bricks in taekwondo demonstrations, or for crushing a strong opponent in a match or game. For breaking objects in daily life, use '부수다' or '깨다'.

examples.en: I'm going to an orchestral concert this weekend.
The orchestra played a piece by Beethoven.
Listening to orchestral music puts my mind at ease.

examples.ko: 그 작곡가는 관현악을 위한 곡을 많이 썼어요.
examples.en: That composer wrote many pieces for orchestra.

examples.ko: 관현악 편곡 덕분에 노래가 더 웅장해졌어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the orchestral arrangement, the song became more grand.
I was in an orchestra club in college.

explain: 관악기, 현악기, 타악기가 함께 연주하는 음악이나 그 편성을 가리켜요. 일상 대화에서는 '오케스트라'라고 더 많이 말하고, '관현악'은 '관현악단', '관현악곡'처럼 설명이나 공연 안내에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It refers to music played by wind, string and percussion instruments together, or to that kind of ensemble. In daily talk people more often say '오케스트라', while '관현악' appears in words like '관현악단' and '관현악곡' and in concert descriptions.

en: to face off in a match; to compete head-to-head

examples.en: The two teams face off for the first time in the final.

examples.ko: 오늘 두 선수가 세계 대회 결승에서 대전했어요.
examples.en: Today the two players faced each other in the world championship final.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 다음 주에 작년 우승 팀과 대전할 거예요.
examples.en: Our team will play last year's champions next week.

examples.ko: 게임에서 친구와 대전하는 것이 제일 재미있어요.
examples.en: Playing head-to-head against friends is the most fun in games.

examples.ko: 서로 대전한 적이 있어서 상대의 실력을 잘 알아요.
examples.en: We have faced each other before, so I know my opponent's skill well.

examples.ko: 같은 조에서 대전하게 되어서 너무 떨려요.
examples.en: We ended up facing each other in the same group, and I'm so nervous.

explain: 스포츠나 게임에서 상대와 맞붙는다고 할 때 써요. 말로는 '붙다', '경기하다'가 더 자주 들려요. 도시 이름 '대전'과 소리가 같으니 문장을 보고 구분해요.
explain_en: It is used when you go up against an opponent in sports or games. In speech, '붙다' and '경기하다' are heard more often. It sounds the same as the city name '대전', so use the sentence to tell them apart.

dis.h: face off in a match; formal

p.n: The replacement is more colloquial and dramatic.

examples.en: I drew the pattern to embroider on the bag myself.

examples.ko: 이 도안대로 뜨개질하면 쉽게 만들 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you knit following this pattern, you can make it easily.
I downloaded a free pattern from the internet.
The design is complicated, so it's hard to color in.

examples.ko: 케이크 위에 올릴 도안을 골라 보세요.
examples.en: Please pick a design to put on top of the cake.
Place the pattern on the fabric and trace it.

explain: 만들거나 그리기 전에 준비하는 밑그림이나 설계도를 말해서, 뜨개질·자수·색칠 공부·공예에서 많이 써요. 완성된 '디자인' 전체보다는 따라 그리거나 따라 만드는 그림이라는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is the base drawing or pattern prepared before making or drawing something, so it is common in knitting, embroidery, coloring books and crafts. It feels less like a finished 'design' and more like a drawing you follow.

examples.ko: 거리에서 한 아저씨가 아코디언을 연주하고 있어요.
examples.en: A man is playing the accordion on the street.

examples.ko: 아코디언 소리를 들으니 유럽 여행이 생각나요.
examples.en: Hearing the accordion reminds me of my trip to Europe.
I signed up for an accordion class.

examples.ko: 할아버지가 젊었을 때 아코디언으로 노래를 반주하셨대요.
examples.en: I heard Grandpa used to accompany songs on the accordion when he was young.
This piece is played on accordion and guitar.
It's a house with a door that folds like an accordion.

explain: 외래어 표기는 '아코디언'이에요. 악기를 말할 때는 '아코디언을 연주하다'처럼 '연주하다'와 자주 써요. 주름이 접히는 모양 때문에 '아코디언 문', '아코디언 커튼'처럼 비유로도 써요.
explain_en: The standard spelling of this loanword is '아코디언'. For the instrument it commonly goes with '연주하다', as in '아코디언을 연주하다'. Because of its folding pleats, it is also used figuratively in '아코디언 문' and '아코디언 커튼'.

examples.en: The students recite a poem in the classroom.

examples.ko: 저는 그 시를 처음부터 끝까지 암송할 수 있어요.
examples.en: I can recite that poem from beginning to end.

examples.ko: 선생님이 앞에 나와서 암송해 보라고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher told us to come to the front and recite.
The child reciting the multiplication table was cute.

examples.ko: 어제 외운 문장을 친구 앞에서 암송했어요.
examples.en: I recited the sentences I memorized yesterday in front of my friend.
I attend a group where we recite Bible verses.

explain: '외우다'는 머릿속에 기억하는 일이고, '암송하다'는 외운 것을 소리 내어 말하는 일까지 포함해요. 그래서 시, 구구단, 기도문처럼 말해서 들려주는 것에 잘 어울려요. 일상 대화에서는 '외워서 말하다'라고도 많이 해요.
explain_en: '외우다' is about fixing something in memory, while '암송하다' includes saying it aloud. So it suits things you say for others to hear, like poems, the multiplication table or prayers. In everyday talk people also say '외워서 말하다'.

examples.en: Prize money is given to the prizewinners of the contest.
The list of prizewinners is posted on the website.
Among this year's prizewinners, there is even an elementary school student.
The prizewinners are invited to the award ceremony next week.
Unfortunately, I didn't make it among the prizewinners.
Everyone was nervous on the day the prizewinners were announced.

explain: '입상하다'(상위에 들어 상을 받다)와 짝으로 알아 두세요. '우승자'는 1등을 가리키지만 '입상자'는 등수 안에 들어 상을 받은 사람들을 두루 말해요. 대회, 공모전, 시상식 이야기에서 자주 써요.
explain_en: Learn it as a pair with '입상하다' (to place and win a prize). '우승자' refers to the first-place winner, while '입상자' covers everyone who placed and received a prize. It is used often when talking about contests, competitions and award ceremonies.
